value.quote: We provide NP-Hardness results for electing an ideal set of representatives
value.note: AL: NP-hardness results. WD: rules evaluated against the majority-agreement objective. SI: simulations, which make up most results. OT: proposal of the FRD model, a main contribution of the paper.

C1.reason: The paper's introduction of FRD as a new voting-system model is a main contribution, so OT applies alongside AL, WD and SI.

value.quote: voters’ preferences over candidates are derived exactly from their agreement
value.note: Issue preferences (v_j, P_V) and electoral inputs (P_VC) are separate objects with separate notation. The paper notes that the derivation assumption should be relaxed, so the two may differ.

C2.4.reason: Held issue preferences and submitted electoral inputs have separate notation, and the link between them is an explicit assumption the paper says could be relaxed.

value.quote: we assume that v approves of c if and only if
value.note: Reported approvals and rankings are stated in words to follow exactly from voters' issue agreement.

C3.2.reason: The paper explicitly states that reported approvals and rankings follow exactly from held issue preferences.

value.quote: We give the election rules the best chances we can
value.note: The reason given is that this is a best-case assumption for the election rules.

C3.3.reason: The stated justification is a best-case assumption for the rules, which fits none of the listed reason categories.

value.quote: each voter v j is assigned a preference intensity parameter
value.note: Intensity for voters is used, so C4.1 applies. Intensity defines the Bernoulli parameter of issue preferences and the delegation probability. Rankings and approvals are defined from agreement L(v,c).

C4.1.reason: Voter preference intensity is used, so the item applies, and its relation to the inputs is formally defined.

value.quote: We hold Direct Democracy with majority voting and full participation
value.note: Majority agreement is evaluated against voters' issue preferences, which are separate from the submitted electoral inputs.

C5.2.reason: Outcomes are evaluated against voters' issue preferences, which are defined separately from the electoral inputs submitted to the rule.

value.note: Elected representatives act as proxies receiving delegations; the codebook places delegates and proxies under VOT.

C6.OTH.reason: Representatives in FRD function as proxies, which the codebook assigns to VOT rather than OTH.

value.note: Only one type (VOT, including representatives as proxies) is present.

C7.1.reason: With representatives coded under VOT, fewer than two types are present.
